To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the coherent effects on the two-pion interferometric analysis are significant in ultra-high energy (UHE) heavy-ion collisions, and the two kinds of coherent effects can be distinguished from each other by analyzing the pion spectra in the momentum range from 0.2 GeV to 2.5 GeV.
the wave packet length and the radius of coherent source both decrease the apparent radius and cause abundant pion at low momentum.
the coherent lengths can decrease and even reverse the source size extracted from the Hanbury-Brown-Twiss radius.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the coherent lengths on the two-pion correlation function in the ultra-high energy heavy ion collisions.
the influence of coherence effects in the production of two-pion interferometer.
the effects of the coherent lengths on two-pion correlation functions and the effects of the wave packet length on the Hanbury-Brown-Twiss (HBT) interferometry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coherent effects can be important in the analysis of two-pion interferometric results in ultra-high energy collisions, but they are not the main cause of the observed large source radii.
the two-pion correlation function is sensitive to the wave packet length but insensitive to the radius of the source.

coherent effects in the source and in the wave packet can be distinguished by the different behavior of the radii of the source and of the Gaussian widths of the pions in the transverse momentum distributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two-pion interferometric radii and the extracted HBT parameters are not reliable for the study of space-time evolution in heavy-ion collisions if the coherent lengths are not taken into account.
the two-pion interferometric method can not be used to measure the size of the source in ultra-high energy collisions.

the coherent length of the wave packet can be used to describe the pion production mechanism and the coherent length of a source can be used to characterize the source structure in heavy-ion collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coherent length should not be ignored when analyzing the data from the future high-energy heavy-ion collisions.
the apparent radius of a source in ultra-high energy (UHE) heavy-ion collisions is smaller than that in lower energies.
the coherent lengths should be taken into account in two-pion interferometric analyses.
